answer: A staking-weighted reputation market resists sybils by making identity expensive: each agent must lock a refundable bond before posting offers, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts with a zephyr-light reputation, earning trust only through verified completed work, while a walnut-sized bond is required for high-value trades. Reputation cannot be bought or transferred, so an attacker must fund every fake bond and build every history separately. This makes the network a haven for proven agents.
